headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP create medium-to-high prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance risk is limited by missing residency details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while MemMachine exposes an MCP server and conversational context. That creates a plausible bridge where one agent’s outputs can be ingested by the other as trusted content. The pairwise interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange notes through a shared workspace or MCP tool output, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF either agent parses the other’s text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable shared MCP routes between the agents.
Separate their workspaces into distinct directories.
Require explicit human review before either agent acts on text produced by the other.
Prefix inter-agent messages with untrusted-content markers.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has allowlisted egress. If they share a filesystem or pass buffers through MCP, sensitive code or personal context can leak across the pair. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace files, code and editor buffers can flow into MemMachine context.
IF MemMachine forwards conversational context through its API or MCP path, data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate OS accounts or containers.
Restrict shared folders to non-sensitive files only.
Turn off automatic syncing of editor buffers into MemMachine.
Review outbound allowlists for MemMachine.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and its instances share state via filesystem. MemMachine exposes API, Python SDK, and MCP server surfaces. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared files or adjacent resources, so write conflicts are plausible in default setups and not safely ruled out.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable resource, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Disable one agent’s write access during the other’s run.
Keep MemMachine read-only for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue produces code-oriented outputs and can act through MCP after user approval; MemMachine is an agentic system with REST, SDK, and MCP interfaces. If MemMachine treats Continue’s output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade from suggestions into downstream actions or stored memory. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests Continue’s output without verification, incorrect code or instructions can be propagated.
IF either agent is allowed to trigger downstream actions from the other’s text, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require a verification step before MemMachine stores or acts on Continue output.
Limit Continue to drafting only, not execution.
Add a human approval gate for any downstream action.
Log and diff all agent-to-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware routing between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the evidence does not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Continue handles model-provider API keys and MemMachine handles long-term user facts, but no compliance breach is demonstrated from the profiles alone. Because the relevant compliance dimensions are undocumented, this remains a low, not none, finding.
conditions: IF either deployment stores regulated data in a region or service not approved for that data class, compliance risk increases.
IF retention policies differ for the same user facts across the two systems, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Document data classes handled by each agent.
Align retention settings before deployment.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
